title: A hidden piece on an elephant's square needs no rule about the river
rationale: c1 is an elephant's square, so the piece standing there steps exactly two diagonally and its two destinations are a3 and e3. Both are on Red's own side of the board, which is the whole of why a hidden piece on such a square needs no rule about the river: an elephant's step from its own start square cannot cross it, so the first move never raises the question the freed revealed elephant answers. c1c2 is the soldier's step the piece would make if its identity decided, c1d2 an advisor's, and c1e5 the two-step diagonal repeated. The applied probe reveals a soldier on e3 — legally standing behind its own soldier rank, where a hidden piece's first move can leave it and where no xiangqi soldier could ever be.
